_doc: MANAGERS-1: the one register of managers a system runs. Every system made from the seed carries this file; the tick's reconcile step (worker/src/managers.js) hires every manager that is on and has no runtime row, the dispatch step skips a manager that is off, and the bootstrap hires from the same list. A deployment with different needs changes `switch` only: {"<manager id>": {"state": "off", "reason": "..."}}. A core manager cannot be switched off; an off switch needs a reason; with no switch every manager is on, which is the safe default (an idle manager costs one small read per tick; a missing manager leaves its items undispatched). tick_every and count equal seed/ultrastable.json roles (checked by `python3 -m foundation managers --check` on the platform). Ultrastable is the foundation for any autonomous system.

managers.for: allocation across every project; the tick heartbeat. Every system has one.
delivery of one outcome: triage, done checks, closing items.
the backlog a bare idea does not come with: growth, measures, scouting, improvement items.
independent verification of every claimed result.
the tick, workflows, budgets, deploys and settings.
funding registry and applications. Switch off for a system whose owner pays its running cost and seeks no funding.
introducing the work to organizations. Switch off for a private or personal system with no public audience.
the outreach calendar and the social queue. Switch off together with the outreach manager.
research and white papers. Switch off for a system that publishes no findings.
story, site copy, search and social presence. Switch off for a system with no public front end to promote.
licence, notices and third-party licence compliance. Switch off only for a system that ships no code or content to others.
onboarding and support intake. Switch off for a system with one user who is its owner.
which managers this system runs: keeps this register true and hires what is switched on.
sequencing across projects under the portfolio constraint; deploy-raising and cost-cutting work first when k is under its floor.
hosting resources, bindings, cost budgets and deploys.
the design language and its experiments. Switch off for a system with no user interface.
the audited front end and its user paths. Switch off for a system with no user interface.
